name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,441

clue.text: Condescend to include son in plan

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: to deign is to condescend to do something
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A haughty person reluctantly agrees to make room for their son in some scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a scheme or intention, as in a plan drawn up for a building or a purpose in mind.

clue.text: Insensitive clique? Absolutely

blocks.note: dead means numb, without feeling
a set is a group of like-minded people

explanation.surface: A question about an uncaring social circle is answered with a firm yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead set, in British and Australian usage, is an emphatic way of saying completely or definitely.

clue.text: Minor issues raised over pedestrian shopping area

indicators.note: in a down answer raised means lifted upward, so the word reads from bottom to top
over here means spread across and round, so the turned word encloses the next

blocks.note: to issue is to emit
a mall is a traffic-free shopping precinct

explanation.surface: Small problems are brought up concerning a walking-only shopping precinct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pedestrian' suggests dull, but here it means for walkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-time describes an operator of little importance, a minor or petty player.

clue.text: Easily imposed on Sweden's environmentalists

blocks.note: green means naive, easily duped
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Swedish ecological campaigners are said to be pushovers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greens are members of ecological political parties, campaigning to protect nature.

clue.text: Complains about Wally not following arrangements for commuters

indicators.note: F is the abbreviation for following, so 'not following' asks for that letter to be dropped
about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

blocks.note: to carp is to complain pettily
a wally is British slang for a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: Someone moans about an idiot who refuses to go along with the travel plans for the daily commute.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally is British slang for an idiot; F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references.
explanation.definitionFit: Car pools are schemes where several workers share one vehicle for their daily journey to the office.

clue.text: Fellow American getting angry when upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means tipped up, so the word is read from the bottom

blocks.note: A is an abbreviation for American
mad means angry

explanation.surface: An American man grows furious when things go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam is a man's name, and crosswords often take a name as a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam, the first man in Genesis, gives a male name, and a fellow is a man.

clue.text: Pass through Portugal before receiving something to eat

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so the word holds the food inside

blocks.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
ere is an old word for before
meat is food

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses Portugal and stops for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To permeate is to spread through or penetrate a substance or space.

clue.text: Overcome when dismissed by Rob

blocks.note: a batter is out when dismissed in cricket
to do someone is slang for to cheat or rob them

explanation.surface: A batter is overcome after being dismissed by a bowler called Rob.
explanation.walkthrough: Rob looks like a name, but it is the verb to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass or beat them, overcoming them in a contest.

clue.text: Affair with Noah's son not ending completely

indicators.note: not ending tells us the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: Shem was one of Noah's three sons
bang means exactly or completely, as in bang up to date

explanation.surface: A romantic affair involving one of Noah's sons never quite finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebang is an affair or business, as in the whole shebang, meaning the entire matter.

clue.text: Greatly surprised by a confusing mass of information on Germany

blocks.note: taken as written
a maze is a bewildering network, here of facts
D is the international vehicle code for Germany; 'on' places it after

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished by a bewildering pile of data about Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: To be amazed is to be filled with astonishment and wonder, the state of being greatly surprised.

clue.text: Artist's wife possessing strength of character

indicators.note: something possessing another thing holds it within, so one word takes the other inside

blocks.note: a mate is a spouse or partner
grit is courage and resolve

explanation.surface: A painter's wife is admired for her determination.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking the artist to the wordplay rather than marking possession.
explanation.definitionFit: René Magritte was the Belgian surrealist painter known for bowler-hatted men and a pipe that is not a pipe.

clue.text: Do for retiring salesman taking shape

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going backwards, so the word is reversed

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
form means shape

explanation.surface: A party is held for a salesman about to retire who is in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform is to do or carry out an action or task.

clue.text: Nothing to like about German novelist

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the opening words are read from the end

blocks.note: nil means nothing, zero
as in 'as good as' means like
Ger is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: Someone finds nothing to like in a German novelist's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns round both opening words as a unit, not just one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: J. D. Salinger was the American writer of The Catcher in the Rye.

clue.text: City centre of Bonn featured in TV crime drama

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, so only the inner part is kept
something featured in a show appears within it, so it goes inside the other word

blocks.note: Vera is a British ITV detective series
the two middle letters of the city name

explanation.surface: The middle of a German city appears in a television detective show.
explanation.walkthrough: Vera is a long-running British TV detective drama set in Northumberland.
explanation.definitionFit: Verona is a city in northern Italy, famous as the setting of Romeo and Juliet.

clue.text: Rector involved in new appeal for clothing

indicators.note: being involved in something places one inside it
new suggests a fresh version, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: A vicar takes part in a fresh fundraising drive for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for clothes and garments.

clue.text: End of story on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so the sound counts and not the spelling

blocks.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: The conclusion of a story broadcast on radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of story' reads as one phrase, but End is the definition and story the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail is the rear or final part of something, as in the tail end of a queue.

clue.text: Unsatisfactory part of McIlroy's game is disconcerting

blocks.note: off means below standard, as in an off day
Rory McIlroy is a Northern Irish golfer, and putting is part of golf

explanation.surface: A golf commentator notes that weak work on the greens is troubling for the star player.
explanation.walkthrough: Rory McIlroy is a famous Northern Irish golfer; putting is striking the ball towards the hole on the green.
explanation.definitionFit: Something off-putting unsettles or deters people, so it is disconcerting.

clue.text: Involve Independent politician at first looking into climate change

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the preceding word
looking into something means being inside it
change signals that the word should be rearranged

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for Independent
the opening letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Independent politician starts investigating climate change.
explanation.walkthrough: I comes first; P goes into a rearrangement of climate.
explanation.definitionFit: To implicate someone is to show them to be involved in something, usually a crime.

clue.text: Told to go to pick up rubbish around grating

indicators.note: picking something up takes it inside, so one word holds the other
around means turned round, so the word is reversed

blocks.note: someone sent away has been told to go
dirt is rubbish, filth

explanation.surface: Someone was ordered to collect litter from around a drain grating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grating' looks like a drain cover at the end of the instruction, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident sound is harsh and rasping, just as a grating noise is.

clue.text: Uncommonly loud girl drinking wine with soldiers

indicators.note: someone drinking takes something in, so the name swallows the other letters

blocks.note: Sian is a Welsh girl's name
tent is a deep red Spanish wine
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A noisy young woman is drinking wine in the company of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is an old name for a Spanish red wine, and other ranks are soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A stentorian voice is extremely powerful, named after Stentor, the loud-voiced herald of the Trojan War.

clue.text: Remain valid for Brown following conclusion of discussions with Unionists

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: the last letter
tan is a brown colour
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown's position holds after talks with Northern Irish Unionists end.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown suggests Gordon Brown, the former British prime minister, but it is the colour; 'following' places it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument or claim that stands up holds good under scrutiny and remains valid.

clue.text: Identify a moral flaw

blocks.note: first meaning: to notice or pick out
second meaning: a blemish on one's character

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to find a failing; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to pick out or recognise; as a noun it is a stain or blemish on a reputation.

clue.text: Because of that article about extremes of bigotry ...

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: the definite article
re means about, concerning
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on prejudice, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this clue to the next to make one sentence, but each is solved alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereby means by that means or as a result of that.

clue.text: ... German fellow gets shot

blocks.note: G is an abbreviation for German
Lance is a man's name

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a German man is shot as a result of bigotry.
explanation.walkthrough: A glance is a cricket stroke deflecting the ball off the bat's face.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a glance is a shot that deflects the ball fine with an angled bat.

clue.text: Severely criticise wife leaving to sing carols at Christmas

indicators.note: the wife leaving means her letter departs from the word that follows

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
to wassail is to go from house to house singing carols

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a wife who walks out on the family carol singing.
explanation.walkthrough: WASSAIL loses its W for wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack vigorously, including with words, so it means to criticise harshly.

clue.text: Returned unaltered by London's top rope maker

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the phrase reads from the end
the top of a down entry is its first letter

blocks.note: as is means unchanged
the first letter

explanation.surface: A London rope maker sends goods back unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a plant fibre traditionally twisted into rope and twine.

clue.text: Want to be emotionally affected by the same thing

definitions.text: be emotionally affected by the same thing

blocks.note: first meaning: to fancy or desire, as in fancying a drink

blocks.clueFragment: be emotionally affected by the same thing
blocks.note: second meaning: to share the same feelings as someone else

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a playful reading: to feel alike, sharing the same emotion as another.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to desire something, as in fancying a cup of tea, and also to share someone's feelings.

clue.text: Covers up ignoring Mark's requests

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: to mask is to cover up or hide
M is the abbreviation for mark, a former German currency

explanation.surface: Someone conceals things while disregarding Mark's pleas.
explanation.definitionFit: Asks as a plural noun means requests or demands, as in a big ask.

clue.text: Give out a variety of seeds in Palau's capital

indicators.note: a variety is a mixed assortment, so the letters are jumbled into a new order
a capital is a first letter, so only the opening letter of the island name counts

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
Palau is a Pacific island nation

explanation.surface: Someone hands out an assortment of seeds in the chief town of a Pacific island state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does double work here as fodder; the fodder is SEEDS, IN and P together.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense is to distribute or hand out, as a pharmacist dispenses medicine.

clue.text: Stupid letters from Helena's niece sent back

indicators.note: letters from a piece of writing are found inside the following words
something sent back travels the other way, so the run is read backwards

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Silly correspondence from a relative is returned to sender.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Helena's niece' backwards and the answer appears across the join of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Insane is used loosely to mean wildly foolish or senseless, as in an insane idea.

clue.text: Most cultivated Europeans admitting - it takes time

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the nationality takes the next word inside it

blocks.note: Poles are people from Poland
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Refined continental people concede that something requires patience.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite once meant refined or civilised, so the most polite society is the most cultivated.

clue.text: Odd parts of essay on goddess ultimately dismissed as contrary to usual belief

definitions.note: the clue gives an adjectival phrase; the answer is the noun for such a view

indicators.note: odd parts are the first, third and fifth letters of the word that follows
ultimately points to the last letter, and dismissed throws it out

blocks.note: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods
letters one, three and five

explanation.surface: An essay about a goddess is rejected for going against accepted doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: HERA loses its last letter, and the odd letters of essay go after it, as 'on' places them.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is an opinion or doctrine at odds with what is orthodox or generally accepted.
